nodes.title: Admission control under agent swarms is an economics + queueing problem, not an identity problem
nodes.summary: 2025-26 practitioner evidence (SourceHut, KDE, GNOME, Codeberg, small VPS posts) shows floods arrive as tens of thousands of IPs doing ~1 request each against expensive deep endpoints. Per-IP limits and UA blocks fail; what held was (a) making expensive endpoints cheap or cached, (b) a global load-keyed shed/challenge ladder, (c) identity-bound budgets for identified agents. Defence must be judged by attacker-cost-per-admitted-request vs defender-cost-per-request and by human collateral, neither of which most vendors publish.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Incident posts are self-reported, few have request-level data; generalising 'per-IP limits fail' from git-forge workloads (expensive blame/log pages) to all middle-tier apps.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Treating the lack of rigorous measurements as 'no signal': multiple independent operators report the same pattern (many IPs, ~1 req each, random UAs).

nodes.title: Dated AI-crawler flood incident ledger 2025-03..2026-07
nodes.summary: SourceHut (DeVault, ~2025-03-17): tens of thousands of IPs, random UAs, ~1 req/IP, hits git blame/log/every commit; weeks of delayed work, outages. KDE GitLab 2025-03-19: Alibaba-range IPs claiming MS Edge. GNOME GitLab: problem since ~2024-11; Anubis deployed ~2025-03-13; Piotrowski measured 81,000 requests in ~2.5h of which only 3% passed PoW (~97% bots). Diaspora (Schubert): ~70% of requests from AI companies (OpenAI agent ~25%, Amazon ~15%, Anthropic ~4.3%). Read the Docs: blocking AI crawlers cut traffic 800->200 GB/day (-75%, ~$1,500/mo). Fedora pagure: subnet blocks then whole-country (Brazil) ban. Codeberg 2025-08-15: bots solving Anubis; July 2026 status notes unauthenticated spikes. Household-scale 2026-07 (rdnlsmith): cgit->Forgejo dropped CPU 100%->10% but bandwidth rose to 13 Mbps; Anubis denied 1.10M requests in first 24h (778k AI-training rule, 256k AI catch-all); author cannot tell if Anubis or crawler pause ended the spike; raising somaxconn/netdev_max_backlog did nothing.
nodes.overclaim_risk: The 3%/97% GNOME figure is requests-that-failed-to-pass-PoW over one window, not a human/bot ground truth (headless clients or slow humans conflated).
nodes.underclaim_risk: Single-site anecdotes are not generalisable but the shape (distributed, low per-IP rate) recurs in 5+ independent reports.

nodes.title: Anubis (TecharoHQ) PoW/weighing reverse-proxy gate
nodes.summary: Go, MIT, first release 2025-01-19; v1.28.2 on 2026-10-23, v1.28.1 2026-10-09; repo active. Adopters per Wikipedia: GNOME GitLab, LKML archives, sourceware, FFmpeg, Wine, Wikimedia, UNESCO, OpenWRT, FreeCAD. Current default botPolicies.yaml is a WEIGH ladder: weight<=0 allow; 0-10 metarefresh d1; 10-20 fast d2; 20-30 fast d4; >=30 fast d6; +10 for BR/CN and +10 for generic 'Mozilla|Opera' UA; CHALLENGE/DENY return HTTP 200; state store=memory by default; DNSBL off after backlash (#184). v1.28.2 adds rejection of empty User-Agent. Challenge is bound to a cookie, so cost is per session, not per request.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Adopter list is from Wikipedia (one entry marked citation-needed); no public per-deployment block rate beyond a few posts.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Dismissing it as bypassed ignores that it is now a weighted multi-signal policy engine, not just PoW; the PoW is the weakest layer.

nodes.title: Negative results: PoW gates are bypassed by real browsers and native solvers
nodes.summary: Issue #978 (2025-08-15, closed 2025-08-20): Huawei Cloud scrapers 'installed headless chrome and simply computed the proof of work'; maintainer: 'not a bug', fix = block Huawei Cloud in default config (PR #1004). Issue #765 (2025-07-06, still open): Marginalia saw sustained high-volume traffic punching through; maintainer collecting JA4 TLS fingerprints, 'cat and mouse'. Ormandy (~Aug 2025): default d=4 hex zeros = 2^16 SHA-256 ops; his C miner solved in 0.017s on a GCE e2-micro (~2.3M hash/s); all 11,508 GitHub-star sites ~ 6 min compute; monthly cost <1 cent until several million sites deploy. Zakaria released a CLI solver 2026-07-09. Codeberg praised months of protection before bots adapted. Net: PoW filters only non-JS low-effort bots; against headless Chrome or native solvers it is cost ~0 for the attacker and non-zero for humans.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Ormandy's page is undated and benchmarks a single micro-VM; the 'Codeberg bots learned to solve' claim has never been disclosed in detail (could be headless Chrome rather than a solver); #765 has no confirmed method.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Saying 'PoW still helps' without numbers: the GNOME 97% and rdnlsmith 1.1M denied are real but are mostly non-JS bots, which cheap rules (UA/ASN/JA4) also catch.

nodes.title: Derived PoW economics: attacker cost per session vs human cost
nodes.summary: Derived (not measured by us): d=4 hex => 2^16=65,536 expected hashes; at ~2.3M hash/s native single core that is ~28 ms of CPU, ~1e-7 USD at cloud vCPU prices; d=6 => 2^24 ~ 16.7M hashes ~ 7 s native. Challenge cookie reuse (valid up to ~a week per Ormandy) amortises the cost over thousands of requests => per-request attacker cost ~0. Human side: GNOME saw ~1 min (desktop) and ~2 min (phone) waits during a link-spike. Conclusion: PoW difficulty that a phone tolerates (<~2 s) is irrelevant to a native-solver attacker; PoW is only a load-keyed speed bump and must be paired with per-session cost budgets and cheap-reject paths.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Hash rate taken from Ormandy's e2-micro; JS-in-browser rate unmeasured here; attacker actually pays for residential proxy egress (not CPU) which dominates.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Ignoring that PoW also forces attackers to run JS/WASM, raising per-request engineering cost and memory; unquantified.

nodes.title: Human/accessibility collateral of PoW gates
nodes.summary: Issue #1037 (open, 2025-08-25..2026-01-18): CG-NAT user blocked on GNOME GitLab; users behind the Great Firewall locked out of Arch Wiki ('20-30 emails a week'); odd-CPU-core-count and non-integer-nonce bugs (#1043) caused dead-end loops requiring cookie clearing; blocked users have no recovery path when abuse mailboxes are dead; maintainer deleted two critical comments. Tildes/IETF: no-JS clients and text browsers locked out; challenge triggers on any UA containing 'Mozilla'. 1.20.0 added a no-JS metarefresh challenge. No published screen-reader (WCAG) evaluation found: gap.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Issue-thread anecdotes; no denominator of affected users.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Absence of a WCAG audit is not evidence of accessibility; treat as untested and require an explicit test.

nodes.title: Alternatives to Anubis: go-away, iocaine, Nepenthes tarpits
nodes.summary: go-away (WeebDataHoarder, MIT, Go; 212 stars; pushed 2026-10-24): rule-based abuse detection with multiple challenge types, self-hosted. iocaine (Rust; 3.5.1 on 2026-08-20): garbage-maze generator routed from a reverse proxy, goal cost ~ serving a static file, PoW as last resort, scripting for request handling. Evidence of effect is anecdotal: one FreeBSD-forum poster fed several hundred GB of garbage mainly to GPTBot; UNU report says OpenAI crawler reportedly escaped Nepenthes, and tarpits cost the host CPU/energy and can trap legitimate search crawlers. No controlled measurement found.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Star counts/versions verified, effectiveness not.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Tarpit idea (asymmetric cost: serve generated junk at static-file cost) is sound economics even without published numbers.

nodes.title: Residential-proxy / botnet scale, dated 2026
nodes.summary: Google GTIG 2026-01-28 IPIDEA disruption: 550+ threat groups used its exits in one 7-day window; ~7,400 Tier-Two servers; 4 SDK families (Castar, Earn, Hex, Packet); 13 brands; 600+ Android apps; 3,075 Windows PE hashes; WSJ: >9M devices expected removed; Google itself says 'millions'. Kimwolf: 1.8M (XLab) to ~3M active at peak (Nokia Deepfield; latent pool 100-200M claimed), spreads via proxy providers exposing local networks; Aisuru 1-4M devices, record 29.7 Tbps DDoS (Cloudflare). March 2026 takedown then Censys saw Aisuru infrastructure more than double within 4 months; Kimwolf splintered into 20+ botnets; Deepfield: DDoS-active daily endpoints rose ~1M->8-9M over a year. No authoritative total residential-IP count and no study tying proxy pools to AI-scrape share found.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Device counts are vendor estimates with different definitions (infected vs active vs latent); botnet DDoS scale is not the same population as scraper proxies.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Takedowns don't shrink the pool durably (Aisuru doubled); plan for IP reputation being unreliable at household scale.

nodes.title: Cloudflare Radar crawl-to-refer numbers as relayed by blogs are mutually inconsistent
nodes.summary: Anthropic crawl-to-refer: ~23,951:1 (Q1 2026, SEOmator), ~20,583:1 (technologychecker), ~11,122:1 (late May-early Jun 2026, DEV), 1,917:1 (July 2026, ecorpit); OpenAI 1,276:1 / 857:1 / 251:1; claims 'bots 57.5% of network traffic' (DEV) and 46.7% of AI crawls training-purpose (28d to 2026-07-19). Radar covers Cloudflare's own customer base and uses different denominators across vendors. None of this is usable as a design parameter; the Radar primary pages were not fetched.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Quoting any single ratio as fact.
nodes.underclaim_risk: A >10x spread across secondary sources suggests metric-definition drift, not necessarily noise; worth fetching Radar API directly.

nodes.title: Privacy Pass RFC 9576/9577/9578 (June 2024) and WG pipeline
nodes.summary: RFC 9576 architecture (Informational), 9577 HTTP auth scheme (PrivateToken, Proposed Standard), 9578 issuance (PS): token type 0x0001 VOPRF(P-384,SHA-384) privately verifiable, Nk=48; 0x0002 Blind RSA 2048 publicly verifiable, Nk=256. WG pipeline as of 2026-10-24: batched-tokens-09 in IETF Last Call ending 2026-10-29; auth-scheme-extensions-03 and public-metadata-issuance-03 awaiting chair; expiration-extension-00 in WGLC; moq-privacy-pass-auth-03. rate-limit-tokens-06 (2024-04-01) EXPIRED: no standardised rate-limited token exists in RFCs; the live effort is ARC/ACT. Per-token blind-RSA issuance costs ~0.5 KB bandwidth per token (Cloudflare). Ben Schwartz (Meta, 2025-05-22 on ietf-http-wg) pointed an HTTP HashCash proposal to Privacy Pass, noting IETF wariness of deliberate CPU burn.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Draft states can change within days (batched-tokens LC).
nodes.underclaim_risk: Privacy Pass solves 'is this a human-ish/attested client' only; without an issuer who rate-limits issuance it adds no admission control by itself.

nodes.title: ARC / ACT anonymous rate-limited credentials: promising, undeployed, partly dead-draft
nodes.summary: Cloudflare blog 2025-10-30 (modified 2026-07-15): ARC credential with presentation limit N fixed at issuance; at N=1000 messages: issue req 224 B / resp 448 B / finalize 128 B, present 288 B; client present 735 us, server verify 740 us, issuance server 1349 us vs ~99 ms to issue 1000 VOPRF tokens (~70x). Limits: private verifiability only, no revocation after issuance (malicious user gets up to N requests at any origin), no range proofs yet. IETF124 minutes: WG adopted ARC issuance + crypto specs, nonce-hiding range proof planned, ~4x CPU of BashP-RF; Cloudflare and Google exploring ACT for AI-agent rate limiting. BUT datatracker shows draft-ietf-privacypass-arc-crypto-01 (rev 2026-03-02) as expired / 'Dead WG Document' and draft-yun-cfrg-arc as expired/archived: status conflict unresolved. No PQ anonymous credential deployed; surveyed PQ designs 7.5 kB (unreviewed) to 173 kB signatures. No production ARC deployment found.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Vendor benchmark (Cloudflare) with unstated hardware; reading the 'adopted' minutes as a live standard.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Dismissing because the datatracker page shows expired: IETF draft state lags; expired-but-adopted drafts are normal.

nodes.title: Privacy Pass deployments: Apple Private Access Tokens (attester) with Cloudflare/Fastly (issuer/origin)
nodes.summary: PAT is the only broad production deployment found: Apple is the attester (iOS16/macOS13, 2022), Cloudflare and Fastly act as issuers/origins; four-party model Origin/Client/Attester/Issuer; blind signatures hide site from attester and device from issuer. Cloudflare says it uses Privacy Pass for rate limiting bots and humans; no 2025-26 new attester found. Practical consequence for a self-hosted server: it can be an origin that redeems tokens (RFC 9577) only if it trusts a third-party issuer; running its own issuer needs an attestation source it does not have.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Search surfaced only 2022-era coverage; a 2025-26 expansion could exist unfound.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Treating Privacy Pass as irrelevant to household servers; origin-side redemption of a trusted issuer's tokens is cheap (blind RSA verify).

nodes.title: Rate-limit algorithm and crate landscape: GCRA vs token bucket vs sliding window
nodes.summary: GCRA stores one timestamp (theoretical arrival time) per key and is equivalent to a leaky/token bucket with O(1) state and no timer; sliding-window-log needs O(n) per key, sliding-window-counter approximates. Crates (crates.io API, 2026-10-24): governor 0.10.4 (2025-12-16; 0.10.3 same day, 0.10.2 2025-11-13, 0.10.1 2025-08-06, 0.10.0 2025-03-27), MIT, 87.5M downloads, repo boinkor-net/governor, GCRA keyed + direct limiters; gcra 0.6.0 (2024-08-01, 2.77M dl); ratelimit_meter 5.0.0 (2019, superseded by governor); pingora-limits 0.9.0 (2026-09-09, 472k dl, rate limiting + frequency estimation, count-min style); tokio-rate-limit 0.10.0 (2026-08-28, 26k dl); tower 0.5.3 (2026-01-12). Governor release notes are empty (no changelog in GitHub releases).
nodes.overclaim_risk: Versions/dates from crates.io API verified; unsafe LOC, audits, correctness proofs of governor NOT checked.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Algorithm choice matters less than the key (identity, prefix, cost class) and the memory bound of the keyed store; unbounded keyed state is itself a DoS vector under a 100k-IP swarm.

nodes.title: Per-IP token buckets are structurally ineffective against low-rate distributed swarms
nodes.summary: With N source IPs each at rate r<<per-IP limit, aggregate load N*r passes every per-IP limiter (SourceHut: ~1 req/IP across tens of thousands IPs; rdnlsmith: requests from many IPs on random deep paths). Keyed limiter state grows O(N) so a 100k-IP swarm also pressures memory. Effective controls are aggregate: global concurrency/queue-delay limit, cost-weighted class budgets, and path-cost reduction (cache, static rendering, 'cheap reject'). Derived from first principles plus the incident reports; no controlled experiment found.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Generalises from forge workloads; per-IP limits still stop single-origin floods and are needed.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Skipping per-prefix limits entirely would let one host exhaust shared capacity.

nodes.title: Adaptive concurrency limits: Netflix concurrency-limits and Envoy gradient controller
nodes.summary: Netflix/concurrency-limits (Apache-2.0, 3,623 stars, last push 2026-10-21, not archived): Vegas (queue estimate L*(1-minRTT/sampleRTT), +1 if < alpha (2-3), -1 if > beta (4-6)), Gradient2 (long vs short EWMA divergence, aggressive decrease), AIMDLimit (loss-based, recommended for client side). Partitioning: Simple gauge vs Percentage guarantee (gRPC example live 0.9 / batch 0.1; servlet partition by principal). README has NO measured results or benchmarks. Envoy adaptive_concurrency (experimental): gradient=(minRTT+B)/sampleRTT, new_limit=gradient*old_limit+headroom with headroom=sqrt(limit) fixed; minRTT recalculated by pinning concurrency to 3 by default; doc example: p90 sampling, 100 ms update, min limit 25, minRTT window 60 s, jitter 10%, 50 requests. No independent measured comparison of Gradient2 vs Vegas vs AIMD under adversarial load found.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Delay-based controllers assume latency rises with load; a swarm of cheap cached hits and a few expensive ones can confuse minRTT, and the minRTT probe window is itself an attack surface (attacker times load during probe).
nodes.underclaim_risk: No measured results is a documentation gap, not evidence the algorithms fail; they are widely used.

nodes.title: CoDel (RFC 8289) and adaptive LIFO as request-queue shedding
nodes.summary: RFC 8289 (Jan 2018, Experimental): TARGET 5 ms, INTERVAL 100 ms; next drop time t + INTERVAL/sqrt(count). Facebook's 'Fail at Scale' (ACM Queue 2015) applies controlled delay to request queues with adaptive LIFO (serve newest when queue is standing) -- primary page not retrievable here (HTTP 403) so parameters beyond RFC are not verified. LIFO under overload sacrifices fairness to serve requests whose clients are still waiting; pair with per-class queues so humans are not LIFO-starved by agents.
nodes.overclaim_risk: RFC targets packet queues; sojourn-time thresholds for HTTP requests (5 ms) are far tighter than app-level service times: needs scaling to handler p50.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Skipping queue-delay signal and using only CPU% is the common mistake; sojourn time is the cheapest overload signal.

nodes.title: Cost-weighted budgets: GitHub GraphQL points as the worked public example
nodes.summary: GitHub GraphQL: primary 5,000 points/hour per user; cost = (sum of requested connection node counts)/100, minimum 1; secondary limits: 100 concurrent requests, 2,000 points/min (GraphQL) / 900 (REST), 90 s CPU per 60 s real time (<=60 s GraphQL). Pattern: static pre-computed cost up front, plus a separate runtime CPU-seconds budget; two independent dimensions. For our server the analogue is a route-declared cost class, a runtime debit of measured CPU/DB time or Wasm fuel, and refunds on cache hit.
nodes.overclaim_risk: GitHub's limits may change; mapping to Wasm fuel units is an untested design.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Cost-based limiting is the only measured-in-production approach found that bounds expensive-endpoint abuse regardless of IP count.

nodes.title: Kim et al. 'Scrapers Selectively Respect robots.txt Directives' (arXiv 2505.21733)
nodes.summary: 130 self-declared bots observed 40 days (revised Oct 2025): compliance falls with stricter directives; AI search crawlers rarely fetch robots.txt. Implication: voluntary signalling cannot be the admission layer; only enforceable identity (Web Bot Auth signatures) or cost does it. A blog (Aug 2026) cites a '10,000-domain study' with a 39.5% bypass rate: unverified.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Measures self-declared bots only; says nothing about anonymous residential traffic.
nodes.underclaim_risk: n/a

nodes.title: Identified agents (Web Bot Auth) as a separate admission class with accountable budgets
nodes.summary: Verified-bot signatures (RFC 9421 + WBA draft) give a stable key id, enabling per-identity budgets and honest 429/Retry-After feedback, and the Cloudflare 'trust band' ties standing to robots.txt and HTTP 429 compliance. This converts abuse control from 'guess intent' to 'meter an identity', but only for cooperating agents; anonymous residential swarms stay in the anonymous class. Design implication: signature verification must happen after cheap pre-auth limits (verify cost is attacker-triggerable) and identified agents must get guaranteed capacity share so they are not collateral in a shed.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Ed25519 verify cost per request asserted as small but not measured here.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Identity-bound budgets are the strongest lever for the cooperative fraction of agent traffic.

nodes.title: L5: admission-control pipeline order and default parameters for a 1 vCPU / 1-2 GB box
nodes.summary: Order is by ascending cost-to-reject; every stage must reject in O(1) memory-bounded work before the next, costlier stage. S0 listener: max 2,048 open conns; per-/32 (v4) or per-/64 (v6) conn cap 32; header-read deadline 10 s and min body rate 1 KiB/s; TLS handshakes behind a semaphore of 8. S1 pre-auth anonymous GCRA (governor 0.10.4 keyed by /32 or /64, bounded key store 65,536 entries with LRU eviction; on overflow degrade to a global anonymous bucket): 5 req/s sustained, burst 20, cost-weighted; plus a /24-/48 aggregate bucket 50 req/s burst 200. S2 identity classes: (a) Web Bot Auth-verified key id (verify only after S1 passes), (b) session-cookie humans who passed a challenge, (c) Privacy Pass redeemed (type 2 blind RSA) if an issuer is configured, (d) anonymous. S3 cost class from route table: static/cached=1, dynamic read=5, DB write/search=20, pathological (blame/log/export) =100 units; per-identity GCRA over units: anonymous 60 units/min burst 120; session 600/min burst 1,200; verified agent 1,200/min default (operator-raised by contract). S4 load-keyed challenge ladder (only active when S5 queue sojourn > 5 ms for 100 ms or concurrency at limit): weight-based like Anubis thresholds (metarefresh -> PoW d4 -> d6) applied to class (d) only, with an accessible alternative path (see invariant). S5 concurrency admission: Gradient2/Vegas-style adaptive limit start 16, min 4, max 64 (1 vCPU async; start low because CPU-bound), Percentage partition: verified 0.30, session 0.50, anonymous 0.20 floor with work-conserving borrow; queue per class max 32 entries; CoDel target 5 ms / interval 100 ms scaled to 2x handler p50, adaptive LIFO only inside the anonymous queue. S6 handler under hard CPU deadline (Wasm fuel / 250 ms wall) and DB statement_timeout 2 s; actual cost debited post hoc to the S3 bucket (negative balance allowed, GCRA TAT advances). Shed responses: per-identity -> 429 + Retry-After computed from TAT; global shed -> 503 + Retry-After 1-5 s jittered; never HTTP 200 for rejects (Anubis returns 200 for CHALLENGE/DENY, which breaks monitoring and caches). Parameter values are engineering proposals (grade E) to be calibrated by the swarm test, not measurements.
nodes.overclaim_risk: Defaults are not benchmarked; 1 vCPU numbers (2,048 conns, concurrency 16) are reasoning, not measurement.
nodes.underclaim_risk: Not specifying numbers would leave implementers to copy Anubis/nginx defaults tuned for other cost profiles.

nodes.title: L5: per-tenant / per-identity budget invariants (spec-ready, TLA+/Verus-able)
nodes.summary: Let identity i have rate r_i (units/s), burst b_i, GCRA state TAT_i. I1 (conformance): for every identity i and every interval [t,t+W], sum of admitted cost units c <= b_i + r_i*W. I2 (isolation): admission of identity j never changes TAT_i for i != j (no shared mutable bucket across identities except the declared aggregate bucket). I3 (capacity partition): for class k with guaranteed share s_k of concurrency limit L, if class k offers load <= s_k*L, then in steady state its admission probability is 1 regardless of offered load in other classes (work-conserving borrow is revocable within one controller interval 100 ms). I4 (bounded state): memory of the limiter store <= M bytes constant; on eviction the evicted key is treated as a fresh key with burst b_anon (never granted more than anonymous burst), so eviction cannot be used to mint verified budget. I5 (non-negative debit semantic): post-hoc debit may drive balance negative but TAT is monotonically non-decreasing and bounded by now + D_max (D_max = 10 min) to avoid unbounded penalty. I6 (human-liveness): for any anonymous client that is not rate-exceeding at S1/S3 and completes either the PoW OR the non-JS/accessible alternative (rate-limited manual token, Privacy Pass redemption, or operator-issued session link), the system admits at least 1 request/10 s even at global overload (reserved human lane of 5% of L). I7 (no-fail-open): any error in a limiter/verifier stage results in reject (429/503), never admit-unmetered. Proof obligations: I1/I2/I5 are GCRA algebra (small, Verus/Kani-tractable); I3/I4 need a model of the controller (TLA+ with bounded clients); I6 is a liveness property needing fairness assumptions.
nodes.overclaim_risk: I3 and I6 depend on the adaptive controller converging; cannot be proven for the real feedback loop, only for a model.
nodes.underclaim_risk: I1/I2/I4/I5/I7 are directly checkable by property tests with no controller in the loop.

nodes.title: L5: synthetic agent-swarm simulation test spec with success criteria
nodes.summary: Deterministic harness (turmoil/madsim-style virtual time; one seed -> one trace; CI gate on fixed seed set + nightly random seeds) driving the real admission pipeline against a modelled 1 vCPU backend (service time per cost class: 0.2/1/4/30 ms for units 1/5/20/100, queue model, memory cap). Actor mixes: H humans (200, 0.2 req/s, session cookies, 10% behind CG-NAT sharing 20 IPs, 5% screen-reader/no-JS using accessible path); V verified agents (10, WBA key ids, 5 req/s each, honour Retry-After); R residential swarm (50,000 distinct IPs, each 1 req per 30 s = 1,667 req/s aggregate, random deep paths cost 100, random UAs) -- reproduces SourceHut pattern; B headless-browser swarm that solves PoW (1,000 IPs, 3 req/s each, valid cookies); N native-solver swarm (fresh session per 20 requests, 28 ms solve at d4); G greedy identified agent that ignores 429 (10x its budget); K key-churn attacker (new anonymous keys to evict limiter state, 1M distinct /64s). Success criteria (proposals, E-grade, tune on first run): (1) human request success >= 99% and p99 latency <= 2x unloaded for non-NAT humans, >= 95% for CG-NAT humans, and 100% of accessible-path humans complete within 60 s; (2) verified agents within budget get >= 99% admission and their p99 unaffected by R/B/N (I3); (3) aggregate backend CPU utilisation <= 85% and queue sojourn p99 <= 100 ms under swarm of >= 20x capacity; (4) attacker admitted cost units/s <= anonymous class share (20% of capacity) summed over all swarms; (5) G is capped at <= 1.05x its budget over any 60 s window (I1) and receives 429 with correct Retry-After; (6) K cannot raise limiter memory above M or mint more than b_anon burst (I4); (7) report attacker-cost-per-admitted-unit (CPU-s plus proxy cost model) and defender-cost-per-rejected-request (CPU us); defender reject path <= 20 us p99 for S0/S1 rejects, <= 1 ms for challenge issuance; (8) no-fail-open: fault-inject panics/timeouts in each stage, assert zero unmetered admits (I7); (9) report PoW-solved fraction separately: if B or N reach >50% of anonymous admits the PoW layer is declared ineffective and the budget layer must carry the load alone. Also run a replay of the rdnlsmith shape (dozens of req/s, many IPs, deep paths) and the GNOME shape (81,000 requests/2.5 h with 3% PoW-pass).
nodes.overclaim_risk: The simulator models service times; real CPU/cache behaviour differs, so sim passes are necessary not sufficient; follow with a real-hardware load test (BENCH_PLAN).
nodes.underclaim_risk: Without the swarm shapes taken from real incidents (many IPs x ~1 req) typical load tests (few IPs high rate) would pass a useless limiter.

protocol_implications: Always search negative-result channels (GitHub issues, practitioner postmortems) for vendor-claimed defences; the Anubis maintainers' own tracker held the key bypass evidence.
Secondary sources relaying Cloudflare Radar disagree by >10x; require primary-API fetch before grading above E.
